paragraphs: R. Yirmeyah deShavshav, Midrash Eikhah, at 'The crown of our head has fallen.' Mattenot Kehunnah suggests that it is a place-name. In the Jerusalem Talmud, end of Sotah, Korban HaEdah explains shivshev as “cut branches,” or alternatively as acting playfully and in a confused manner.. In Kohelet Rabbah, at 'There is an evil I have seen under the sun,' he put a wreath on his head, and Shemuel said of him, ‘It would have been better for him had his head been taken off and he had never done this’ [following the fuller wording in the cited sources and Mattenot Kehunnah]. The story says it came to pass. (See above, R. Berekhya son of R. Simon.)
